knownRisks: AR-01 endedAt offset interpretation is unsettled and sits on the Unit 3 seam: ADR-003 reads AC-19's 'ISO-8601 string with an explicit UTC offset' as UTC with the literal Z designator. A verifier requiring a numeric plus-or-minus HH:MM local offset would find Z insufficient. The code change is trivial but the contract change is not, because Unit 3 inherits whichever is chosen. Must be settled before ENG-03 implements.

AR-02 the score trace is entirely client-produced and every field is forgeable from a browser console; the record attests to nothing and its value is shape, not integrity. No anti-tamper measure was designed into Unit 1 by deliberate decision. The risk was accepted by the product owner in APR-870DC901FD68 and restated in DEC-20260809-001, bounded to Units 1 and 2, with server-side validation required from Unit 3 and to be designed at Unit 3. No workstream may re-accept it.

AR-03 the state signal is a claim by the implementation, not independent proof: a view that never updated data-game-state would not appear in the AC-26 key sweep. ENG-10 must pair the signal with a DOM assertion that no leaderboard, score table, catalogue, settings, profile, lobby or presence view exists in the document.

AR-04 the palette-as-single-source rule is unenforced by tooling; a single hex literal in CSS or in the renderer silently invalidates the AC-16 and AC-17 completeness claim. Mitigation is an automated assertion that no colour literal appears outside src/render/palette.js plus an ENG-01 review item under GATE-CODE-REVIEW.

AR-05 node_modules cannot be git-ignored from inside the write boundary: no root .gitignore exists at the base revision and the repository root is not a writable path, while node_modules is on the contract's own prohibitedPaths. Handling is to never git add it and to build the AC-28 inventory from the workstream commits per WS-01 B-07. If ENG-12 concludes a root .gitignore is necessary, that is a write outside both the narrowed set and the contract's allowedPaths and must be escalated to Product Operations, not created quietly.

AR-06 the opaque-plate and no-tweening rules constrain visual design. If the owner judges the result insufficiently 'modern and colourful' under final_user_visible_acceptance, the remedy is more saturated enumerated palettes and richer motion and shape, not relaxing the opacity or enumeration rules, which would reopen AC-16 and AC-17 completeness. AC-18's judgement half remains the owner's and no engineering workstream can close it.

AR-07 no non-visual representation of gameplay: the canvas is aria-hidden and conveys the play field visually only. No acceptance criterion requires a screen-reader-accessible representation of gameplay. Recorded as a limitation, not as a satisfied requirement.

AR-08 the performance requirement remains unquantified. No numeric frame-rate or input-latency budget exists in any artifact and the contract's NFR is explicitly UNKNOWN. Architecture makes the score frame-rate independent and asserts no budget. Carried open, consistent with WS-01 R-02.

Carried from WS-01 and not resolvable by ENG-02: B-01 (AC-30 needs a runnable command from a clean checkout, and install-time network use must be stated separately from the game's zero network use), B-02 (AC-30's evidence location under .development-os/ read against AC-28's prohibition, which ENG-01 reads as applying to application code and which is a contract defect to escalate if ENG-15 reads it as absolute), and B-05 (AC-21's OS-clock-change procedure may not be executable; the injected clock in ADR-003 section 2 is the inspectable substitute and must be disclosed as a substitute, never reported as the manual procedure).
